subject: Post-call: Aperture Analytics — embeddings fit, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aperture-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Aperture Analytics — embeddings fit, benchmarks, and next steps

Hi Lena / Aperture data team,

Thanks for the time today — appreciated the detailed walkthrough of your semantic search goals and the example queries. Short recap and proposed evaluation path so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: replace keyword search with semantic ranker for clinical notes and support articles (latency target: <= 120ms P95 for query-only flows).
- Data shape: ~3M documents, average doc length ~450 tokens, expected query traffic ~120 qps (spiky).
- Concern areas: recall on short queries, concept drift across specialties, and vector index size/cost.

Redwood quick-recs (post-call):
- Initial embedding candidates: rwd-emb-768-v2 (default), rwd-emb-1024-robust (if cross-specialty variance high).
- Dimensionality tradeoff: 768 dims gives ~20% smaller index; 1024 dims improves mean recall@10 by ~0.8–1.4 pts on cross-specialty tests we ran.
- Quantization note: int8/8bit quant works well for rwd-emb-768 with negligible MRR drop (~0.5 pts) and ~40% storage reduction.

Suggested next steps (timeline):
1) You share a de-identified sample (5k doc subset + 500 queries). We prepared a sample CSV template — attached as aperture-search-sample.csv.
2) Redwood runs a 2-week embedding validation: recall@1/5/10, MRR, latency by model/config, and a drift-sensitivity probe. Deliverable: notebook + CSV report (embed-eval-v0.1.zip).
3) Joint review call (30 min) to pick model and rollout policy + MAP (mutual_action_plan_aperture.pdf).

Open questions for you:
- Can you provide the 5k de-identified sample by EOD Friday (2026-08-22)?
- Any hard constraints on index storage? (e.g., max TB)

Attachments: [attachment: aperture-search-sample.csv], [attachment: mutual_action_plan_aperture.pdf]

I’ll loop Marissa on the evaluation details — she’ll own the benchmarks. If that timeline looks good, I’ll calendar a review for Aug 31.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[vivek@redwood.inference.com]

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aperture-analytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Aperture Analytics (data-team) <data@aperture-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Aperture Analytics — embeddings fit, benchmarks, and next steps

Thanks, Vivek — this is great, and the timeline is doable. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) De-identification: we can remove PHI and provide the 5k sample by Friday. We will keep the doc IDs stable so you can correlate results.
2) Index storage: target is <= 3TB for the core index (we can shard specialties if helpful).
3) Drift concern: we have a quarterly update cadence and are worried about sub-population drift (oncology vs primary care). We’d like a recommendation for a lightweight drift detector we can run daily.

Also, two asks: 
- Can you include recommended prompt templates or query pre-processing for short queries? We saw drop-offs on 2–3 token queries in the demo.
- Any privacy/security redlines before we share the sample? We have a standard DPA in HubSpot (HS-345672).

Appreciate it — looking forward to the eval.

Best,
Lena
Head of Data Platform, Aperture Analytics
[lena.ortiz@aperture-analytics.com]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aperture-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Aperture Analytics — embeddings fit, benchmarks, and next steps

Hi all — jumping in with the technical plan and quick answers to Lena’s questions.

Recommended evaluation checklist (what Redwood will run):
- Models: rwd-emb-768-v2, rwd-emb-1024-robust, and a distilled low-latency candidate rwd-emb-384-lite.
- Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10 (for graded relevance), average cosine distance distribution (to inspect concentration), and latency P95 for embedding generation and kNN search.
- Drift probe: run per-specialty embedding centroid drift + KL on category distributions; alert threshold: centroid cosine shift > 0.02 OR MRR drop > 1.5 pts in sliding 7-day window.
- Dimensionality guidance: start with 768. If you observe specialty-specific recall gaps > 2 pts, test 1024 on that slice — incremental benefit is usually smaller beyond 1024.
- Quantization: test 8-bit quant for the production index. We’ll report MRR delta and index-size reduction in the report.

Prompt/query pre-processing:
- For short queries (1–4 tokens): expand using simple synonyms/aliases (domain lexicon) and prefer retrieval-augmented reranking for the top 50 candidates. Example template we’ll include in the notebook.

Security/ops:
- We’ll only request de-identified samples. Redwood can sign your DPA (HubSpot HS-345672). We don’t need full PHI. Any files you send, please mark the Drive share as view-only.

Deliverables we will push to the Drive link:
- Notebook: evaluation harness + code snippets for incremental testing
- CSV: per-query results including predicted/expected relevances
- Short doc: rollout recommendations and fallback policies for degraded models

I’ve attached a tiny baseline run (embed-eval-v0.1.zip) so you can preview the report format. Vivek — propose we set Aug 31 10:00 PT for the joint review.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
[marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com]

Vivek
